accepted.evidence: Turner 4564 gives Lahnda and Punjabi caṅgā “good” under caṅga. Grierson’s Khetrani survey glosses the elicitation “Good man” but prints only the adjective caŋgā, matching this regional form. Exact LSI digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 11225 gives Lahnda vaḍḍā and western Punjabi vaḍ̠ā “big” under vaḍra, with a “high” use in a neighboring Romani branch. Grierson Khetrani vaḍā is elicited as “High”; this records a local big/high sense without asserting a separate height lexeme. Exact LSI digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

Turner 1634 gives Lahnda uccā “high” and related upper/above uses under ucca. Grierson Khetrani ucā, glossed “Up”, fits the same local upward/high adjective or adverb. Exact LSI digital-edition key and original spelling checked; no import or transcription change.

held.reason: The survey prints an adjective, but a secure precise parent for this local bad/dirty sense remains undetermined.
Potential locative/ground term; avoid a direct opposing derivation from “up” without a lexical source.
